subject.title: Feature: Inject post-install/update system event into active session

question: Should ClawHub/OpenClaw add an automatic active-session post-install/update handoff, and if so what consent and trust gate must run before the agent reads or acts on the newly installed SKILL.md?
rationale: The requested behavior is useful setup UX, but it changes the authority boundary between registry install/update and an active agent session that can run commands or modify configuration.

options.title: Design consent-gated handoff
options.body: Add a post-install/update handoff only after a visible trust prompt or explicit user action, and constrain the agent to verified ClawHub metadata and the installed skill path.

options.title: Keep prompt-only flow
options.body: Continue using copyable OpenClaw install/setup prompts and do not inject events from the ClawHub CLI until a stronger runtime contract exists.

options.title: Allow automatic injection
options.body: Treat install/update as sufficient consent for an active-session system event, accepting the higher security and surprise-cost burden.

recommendation.title: Design consent-gated handoff
recommendation.body: Add a post-install/update handoff only after a visible trust prompt or explicit user action, and constrain the agent to verified ClawHub metadata and the installed skill path.

likelyOwner.reason: They already engaged on this issue and have recent history in the install UX and CLI surfaces that define the boundary under discussion.
